cards.title: Introduction to Vue Testing
cards.content:
Testing is a crucial part of Vue.js development. It ensures your components render correctly, react to user input, and maintain state as expected.

We primarily use Vitest as the test runner and Vue Test Utils to mount and interact with Vue components.

cards.title: Mounting Components
cards.content:
To test a Vue component, you need to mount it using Vue Test Utils.

import { mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import MyComponent from './MyComponent.vue'

const wrapper = mount(MyComponent, {
  props: {
    title: 'Hello Vue'
  }
})

The mount method renders the component and all its child components.

cards.title: Interacting and Triggering Events
cards.content:
You can simulate user interactions using the trigger method on the wrapper element.

test('increments counter on click', async () => {
  const wrapper = mount(CounterComponent)
  
  await wrapper.find('button').trigger('click')
  
  expect(wrapper.text()).toContain('1')
})

cards.title: Order of Writing a Component Test

items: Import the component and test utilities
Find the target element using wrapper.find()
Trigger a user event like click()
Assert the expected output using expect()

cards.title: Summary of Vue Testing
cards.content: You have covered the basics of Vue.js testing! Remember to always await asynchronous updates, use proper assertion libraries, and test user behavior rather than implementation details.
